top_choice_rationale: Base editing is a distinct chemical act on DNA (in-place deamination with no double-strand break) from what the 2020 prize honoured, with a clear mechanism, nucleotide-resolution quantitative evidence, wide reproduction, and a generative capability (single-base correction) now reaching patients. The adenine editor needed an evolved TadA acting on DNA, which is real new chemistry, and attribution to Liu, Komor and Gaudelli follows the sequence of the work; the Kondo/Nishida priority question is a real cost but does not outweigh the rest.
